description: Precalculus, geometry and linear algebra with the computer in hand: functions, limits, vectors and matrices computed and plotted in R and MATLAB as they are learned. Taught to the depth of a first-year linear algebra and precalculus sequence for engineers.
modelledOn: Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications
outcomes: Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions and use them in integration and transforms.
Evaluate limits and test continuity algebraically and numerically.
Model growth, decay and scaling with exponential and logarithmic functions and solve the resulting equations.
Solve problems in coordinate geometry and trigonometry that arise in graphics and navigation.
Compute with vectors and matrices: dot and cross products, systems of equations, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues.
Use R and MATLAB to compute, plot and check every technique in the course.

units.title: Algebra review and partial fractions
topics: Polynomials, factoring, polynomial division, the remainder and factor theorems
Rational expressions and proper versus improper fractions
Partial fractions: distinct linear, repeated linear and irreducible quadratic factors
Applications: summing series, inverse Laplace transforms preview, integrating rational functions
Getting started with R and MATLAB: variables, vectors, plotting

units.title: Functions, limits and continuity
topics: Functions, domain and range, composition and inverses; graphs of standard functions
Limits from tables and graphs; limit laws; limits at infinity and asymptotes
Continuity and the intermediate value theorem; piecewise functions
Numerical estimation of limits in software; floating-point pitfalls
Sequences and convergence

units.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
topics: Exponential growth and decay; the number e; compound interest and mobile-money savings
Logarithms, change of base, laws of logarithms; solving exponential and logarithmic equations
Log scales: decibels, pH, Richter, and plotting algorithm running times
Why log n appears in computer science: binary search, tree height, bits needed

units.title: Geometry and trigonometry
topics: Coordinate geometry: distance, midpoint, lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses
Trigonometric functions, the unit circle, identities, inverse trigonometric functions
Solving triangles: sine and cosine rules; bearings and surveying problems
Polar coordinates and parametric curves
Geometry for graphics: angles between lines, reflection, rotation, areas of polygons

units.title: Vectors
topics: Vectors in 2D and 3D: magnitude, direction, unit vectors, components
Addition, scalar multiplication, linear combinations, span and linear independence
Dot product, angle between vectors, projections; cross product and areas
Lines and planes in space; distance from a point to a plane
Applications: forces, velocities, computer graphics, cosine similarity of documents

units.title: Matrices and systems of linear equations
topics: Matrix notation, addition, multiplication, transpose; special matrices
Systems of linear equations; Gaussian and Gauss-Jordan elimination; row echelon form; rank
Determinants: cofactor expansion, properties, Cramer's rule
Inverse of a matrix; solving AX = B; LU decomposition preview
Matrices as transformations: rotation, scaling, shear; composition of transformations
Markov chains and PageRank as matrix problems

units.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
topics: Characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices
Diagonalisation and powers of a matrix
Applications: population models, vibration, principal component analysis preview
Numerical computation of eigenvalues in R and MATLAB

units.title: Applications in R and MATLAB
topics: Matrix operations, solving systems, determinants, inverses and eigen-decomposition in both tools
Plotting functions, curves, vectors and transformations
Fitting a line to data by least squares as a matrix problem
A capstone: image transformation or a simple recommendation using vector similarity

schedule.title: Polynomials and partial fractions
schedule.exercise: Divide a cubic by a linear factor, use the remainder theorem to test a root, and decompose a proper rational expression with repeated and quadratic factors.

tasks.title: Divide x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6 by x - 3 using polynomial division and check the remainder against direct evaluation at x = 3
Decompose (5x + 3)/((x - 1)(x + 2)) into partial fractions and verify by plotting both forms and comparing values at five points
Decompose (x^2 + 2x + 3)/((x + 1)^2 (x^2 + 4)) into partial fractions, solving for the constants, and verify symbolically

schedule.title: Rational expressions and starting in R and MATLAB
schedule.exercise: Use partial fractions to telescope the sum of 1/(n(n+1)) for n up to 99, and write the commands to plot a rational function with its asymptotes.

tasks.title: Create two vectors in R or Python, compute their sum and element-wise product, and plot y = x^2 for x from -5 to 5
Sum 1/(n(n+1)) for n up to 99 using partial fractions and check against a direct computation in the symbolic tool
Integrate a rational function with an irreducible quadratic factor through partial fractions and compare with a numerical integration at three limits

schedule.title: Functions, limits and continuity
schedule.exercise: Find the domain, range and inverse of three functions, evaluate limits including at infinity, and decide whether a piecewise function is continuous at its joins.

tasks.title: Plot f(x) = 2x + 1 together with its inverse and the line y = x, and confirm the graphs are mirror images
Plot (3x^2 + 1)/(x^2 - 4), find its horizontal and vertical asymptotes, and tabulate values near each to support the limits
Choose constants a and b that make a three-piece function continuous at both joins, and confirm by plotting the completed function

schedule.title: Numerical limits and sequences
schedule.exercise: Show by hand that a_n = (2n + 1)/(n + 3) converges, find its limit, and explain why subtracting nearly equal floating-point numbers loses accuracy.

tasks.title: Print the first 20 terms of a_n = (2n + 1)/(n + 3) and identify the limit they approach
Evaluate (1 - cos(x))/x^2 for x from 1e-1 to 1e-9 and explain the floating-point breakdown at small x
Rewrite a cancellation-prone expression into a stable form, compare both across tiny inputs, and report the relative error of each

schedule.title: Exponentials and logarithms
schedule.exercise: Compute the growth of a mobile-money savings balance with monthly and continuous compounding, solve two exponential equations by logarithms, and state how many bits are needed to index 10 million records.

tasks.title: Plot the balance of 1000 cedis at 8 percent with annual, monthly and continuous compounding for 20 years on one graph
Plot n, n log n and n squared on linear and log-log axes and read off the input sizes where each crosses 1 million steps
Count the comparisons binary search takes on sorted arrays of size 2^k for k up to 20, and verify they match log2 n

schedule.title: Coordinate geometry and trigonometry
schedule.exercise: Find the equation of a circle through three points, verify four trigonometric identities, and solve a surveying problem finding the width of a river using the sine rule.

tasks.title: Plot a circle, a parabola and an ellipse with given equations and read the centre, vertex and foci from each graph
Plot sin^2 x + cos^2 x and tan x against sin x / cos x to verify two identities numerically over 200 points
Compute the width of a river from baseline and two measured angles using the sine rule, and propagate a 0.5 degree angle error

schedule.title: Polar curves and geometry for graphics
schedule.exercise: Convert six points between polar and Cartesian coordinates, sketch the cardioid r = 1 + cos(theta), and rotate a triangle 90 degrees about the origin.

tasks.title: Plot the polar curves r = 1 + cos(theta) and r = 2 sin(3 theta) and count the petals or loops each has
Plot the parametric cycloid x = t - sin t, y = 1 - cos t for t up to 4 pi and mark the arc length of one arch
Compute the area of an irregular plot given by 8 survey points using the shoelace formula, then rotate and reflect it and confirm the area is unchanged

schedule.title: Vectors in two and three dimensions
schedule.exercise: For two given 3D vectors compute magnitude, unit vector, dot product, angle, projection and cross product, and test whether three vectors are linearly independent.

tasks.title: Plot two 2D vectors and their sum from tip to tail, and compute the magnitude and unit vector of each
Compute the angle between two 3D vectors and the projection of one onto the other, and plot both to verify the result
Test whether three 3D vectors are linearly independent using the determinant, and express a fourth vector as their linear combination

schedule.title: Lines, planes and vector applications
schedule.exercise: Find the equation of the plane through three points, the distance from a given point to it, and the cosine similarity between two short documents as word-count vectors.

tasks.title: Write the parametric equation of the line through two 3D points and check a third point lies on it
Find the plane through three points using a cross product, compute the distance from a fourth point, and verify by projecting onto the normal
Represent five short documents as word-count vectors, compute pairwise cosine similarity, and rank the documents most similar to a query

schedule.title: Matrices, linear systems and determinants
schedule.exercise: Solve a 3 by 3 linear system with Gauss-Jordan elimination by hand, state its rank, and check the answer with Cramer's rule.

tasks.title: Multiply two 3 by 3 matrices by hand and confirm the result with the matrix tool, then show AB differs from BA
Solve a 3 by 3 linear system by Gauss-Jordan elimination, listing each row operation, and check the solution by substitution
Determine for which value of k a 3 by 3 system has no solution, one solution or infinitely many, using determinants and rank

schedule.title: Inverses, transformations and Markov chains
schedule.exercise: Find the inverse of a 3 by 3 matrix, apply a rotation followed by a scaling to a triangle, and compute the steady state of a two-state weather Markov chain.

tasks.title: Find the inverse of a 3 by 3 matrix and verify that multiplying it by the original gives the identity
Apply a 45 degree rotation then a scale by 2 to a square and compare the result with the composed matrix applied once
Compute PageRank on a 5-page link graph by power iteration with damping 0.85, and rank the pages by score

schedule.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
schedule.exercise: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 2 by 2 matrix, diagonalise it, and use the result to compute its tenth power for a two-stage population model.

tasks.title: Find the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a given 2 by 2 matrix and verify Av = lambda v for each
Diagonalise a 2 by 2 matrix and use A^10 = P D^10 P^-1 to compute its tenth power, comparing with direct multiplication
Compute the principal component of a 2D dataset through the covariance matrix eigenvectors and plot the data with the principal axis

schedule.title: Computational linear algebra capstone
schedule.exercise: Write up a short report fitting a trend line to ten data points as a least squares matrix problem, and explain how the normal equations produce the coefficients.

tasks.title: Plot a triangle and the result of a shear transformation matrix applied to it on the same axes
Fit a least squares line to ten data points by solving the normal equations and compare the coefficients with a built-in fit
Build a movie recommender from a small ratings matrix using cosine similarity of user vectors, and test it on one held-out rating
